1: {critic} came, saw, and waited forty minutes for a {dish}. 'I've had warmer welcomes from a fridge,' they wrote. Ouch, but fair.
'The {dish} at {restaurant} tasted like it had given up halfway,' says {critic}. Tomorrow is a new day.
{critic} gives {restaurant} one star, and that star is for the comfy chairs.
'I wanted to love it,' writes {critic}. 'The {dish} did not want to be loved.'
2: {critic} found {restaurant} 'friendly but a bit wobbly'. The {dish} needed one more minute of care.
'Good ideas, shaky cooking,' says {critic}. 'Come back in six months and I might be cheering.'
Two stars from {critic}: the {dish} was nearly there, the service was nearly quick.
'There's a good restaurant hiding inside {restaurant},' writes {critic}. 'It just needs to come out and say hello.'
3: {critic} calls {restaurant} 'a solid, honest night out'. The {dish} won't change your life, but it will make your Tuesday.
'Three stars, and a happy tummy,' says {critic}. The {dish} was the highlight.
{critic} liked it: 'Nothing wrong, a few things very right, and a {dish} I'd order again.'
'Reliable as a good umbrella,' writes {critic} of {restaurant}. That's a compliment round here.
4: {critic} is impressed: 'The {dish} at {restaurant} is cooked by someone who really cares.' Bookings are already picking up.
'Go now, before everyone else finds out,' writes {critic}. Too late: everyone has just found out.
Four stars from {critic}, who called the {dish} 'the kind of plate you think about on the bus home'.
'Confident, generous and properly delicious,' says {critic}. Chef {chef} is grinning in the kitchen.
5: FIVE STARS! {critic} says {restaurant} is 'the best meal in {city} this year'. The phone has not stopped ringing.
'I licked the plate. Don't tell my editor,' writes {critic} about the {dish}. Five stars.
{critic} calls chef {chef} 'a genius with a whisk'. Five stars, and a queue down the street by lunchtime.
'Book a table. Book two. Bring your granny,' says {critic}. Five stars for {restaurant}.

inspectorRumours: Someone at table four was taking notes. An inspector? Or just a blogger?
A solo diner took their time and asked about the farm the lamb came from.
A quiet guest in a grey jumper ordered the whole tasting menu and didn't take a single photo.
Someone booked under the name 'Mr Smith'. There are a lot of Mr Smiths in the world, aren't there?
A guest asked whether the bread was made here, then wrote something very small in a very small notebook.
The person at the corner table cleaned their plate, paid in full and left without a fuss. Suspicious? Or just hungry?
A diner asked to see the kitchen 'just out of curiosity'. The whole brigade stood up a bit straighter.
Word from a friend at another restaurant: 'They've been busy round here this month.' Who's 'they'? Nobody will say.
Somebody ordered the same dish two nights apart. Testing for consistency, perhaps?
A guest ate alone, slowly, and asked for the wine list twice. The sommelier is now very nervous.
inspectionSeason: Inspection season has begun. Every service counts from now until guide day.

guideDay.envelope: A thick envelope has arrived from {guide}. Your hands are shaking a little. Open it?
gained: Dear {restaurant}, it is our pleasure to award you {stars} {starWord}. Your kitchen sang all year long. Congratulations!
The guide is delighted to announce {stars} {starWord} for {restaurant}. Chef {chef} may now cry happily into a tea towel.
gainedFirst: Dear {restaurant}, after many quiet visits, we are proud to award your very first star. Welcome to the guide!
One star for {restaurant}! The whole team is jumping up and down in the kitchen. Someone has dropped a whisk.
gainedThird: Three stars. 'Exceptional cooking, worth a special journey.' {restaurant} is now one of the finest restaurants anywhere.
The envelope says THREE. Chef {chef} reads it twice, then sits down on an upturned crate and laughs.
kept: {restaurant} keeps its {stars} {starWord}. Holding on is harder than getting there. Well done, everyone.
Same again: {stars} {starWord} for {restaurant}. The inspectors say the cooking was as steady as a lighthouse.
lost: We're sorry to tell you that {restaurant} now holds {stars} {starWord}. Some nights this year were not quite your best.
The guide has taken a star away from {restaurant}. It stings, but the team that won it is still here. Next year.
lostAll: {restaurant} is no longer in the guide with a star this year. Take a deep breath. Many great kitchens have come back from this.
No stars this year. The kitchen is very quiet tonight. Tomorrow, you start again.
notAssessed: The guide could not assess {restaurant} this year: you were closed for too long. Any stars you held have lapsed.
The inspectors kept knocking, but the doors were shut. Without enough visits, the guide cannot keep your stars.
guideDay.excluded: You asked the guide to leave {restaurant} out this year. The envelope stays sealed, and that's your choice.
stillNone: No star this year, but the guide says it is 'watching with interest'. Keep cooking.
Not this year. The letter mentions your {dish} kindly, though.

fiftyBest.entered: {restaurant} has entered {guide} at number {rank}! Judges around the world are talking about you.
fiftyBest.fell: {restaurant} slips to number {rank} on {guide}. Lists go up and down; the cooking doesn't have to.
fiftyBest.dropped: {restaurant} has dropped off {guide} this year. There are a lot of great kitchens in the world.
fiftyBest.numberOne: NUMBER ONE! {restaurant} is the best restaurant in the world on {guide}. By the rules, you now join the hall of fame and can never be ranked again. You only win this once.
fiftyBest.hallOfFame: {restaurant} sits in the hall of fame of {guide}. Forever number one.

gaultMillau.up: {guide} raises {restaurant} to {points}/20. Their inspectors loved the {dish}.
gaultMillau.down: {guide} lowers {restaurant} to {points}/20. Every half point counts.
gaultMillau.top: {points}/20 from {guide}! They never give 20, so this is about as good as it gets.
gaultMillau.toqueNote: Nobody ever gets 20 out of 20. The guide says perfection is something you chase, not something you catch.

goodFood.listed: {restaurant} is listed in {guide} at level {tier} out of 10.

stressWarning: Chef {chef} has been snapping at the pass and forgot the staff meal. They need a breather.
Chef {chef} is running on coffee and worry. Maybe a quieter week would help?
burnout: Chef {chef} sat down in the walk-in fridge and wouldn't come out. They're going home to rest for a while. The kitchen will wobble.
Chef {chef} has run out of puff. Too many big nights in a row. They'll be back, but not for a few weeks.
wantsOwnPlace: Chef {chef} knocks on the office door. 'I've loved every minute here. But I want my own place. My name over the door.'
'Can we talk?' says Chef {chef}, twisting their apron. 'There's a little site round the corner. I think I'm ready.'
Chef {chef} has been sketching menus on napkins again. 'I want to cook my food,' they say. 'In my own restaurant.'
headChef.backChoice: Back them: help pay for their new place and stay friends. They'll send customers your way.
headChef.letGoChoice: Let them go: wish them well. They might become your biggest rival.
headChef.backed: You backed Chef {chef}. Their new restaurant opens with your name on the thank-you card. The kitchen will miss them.
headChef.leftForRival: Chef {chef} has gone to open a rival restaurant down the road. You taught them everything they know. That's the problem.
headChef.newHeadChef: {chef} steps up to run the pass. Big shoes to fill, but they've been waiting for this.
headChef.rivalStar: Your old head chef's restaurant has earned {stars} {starWord}. You're proud. Mostly.

elBulli.title: Closing at the top
body: Tonight is the last service at {restaurant}.
Every table is full. The kitchen is quiet and calm. Chef {chef} plates the final dessert, and the dining room stands up and claps.
You could have kept going. The bookings were full for a year. But you wanted to stop while every plate was the best it could be.
{restaurant} becomes a foundation: a kitchen for experiments, books and young cooks from all over the world.
Stopping can be winning. You won.

dynasty.title: A legend
body: Three stars, five years in a row.
People travel across oceans to eat at {restaurant}. Young chefs dream of working in your kitchen.
You did it the hard way: night after night, plate after plate. Congratulations.

handedBack.title: On your own terms
body: You handed back your stars and walked away.
No more envelopes. No more mystery diners. Just cooking for people you like.
It's not the ending everyone expected. It's the one you chose.
